t: That the building at 100 Clinton Street, Syracuse, New York (commonly known as the United States Court House and Federal Building), shall hereafter be known, called, and designated as the “James M. Hanley Federal Building”. Any reference in any law, map, regulation, document, record, or other paper of the United States to such building shall be deemed to be a reference to the “James M. Hanley Federal Building”.

fable.w: This section only renames a federal building and directs that existing references be read as the new name. The tempting reading is that the word "regulation" signals rulemaking, but it appears only in a boilerplate list of documents that may mention the building and does not authorize or require any rule. No party outside the federal government is consulted, heard, or given a right to sue over any federal decision.
fable.s: Any reference in any law, map, regulation, document, record, or other paper of the United States to such building shall be deemed to be a reference to the “James M. Hanley Federal Building”.

opus.w: This section only renames a federal building and says that references to it in existing documents will be read as using the new name. The word "regulation" does not authorize any rulemaking. There is no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation, or right to sue, so no one outside the federal government takes part in any federal decision.
opus.b: The only tempting reading comes from the word "regulation." That word only lists documents in which references to the building will be treated as references to the new name. The section does not give anyone authority to write rules, and it involves no outside party.

qwen_chat.w: The section solely designates a specific federal building with a new name and updates legal references accordingly. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or participation with parties outside the federal government, nor does it establish any advisory bodies or public comment periods. The action is a unilateral legislative declaration.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that renaming a building involves public input or consultation, but the text itself contains no such requirement. It is purely a legislative designation.
